title: Structure Formation in Cosmic Voids
bottleneck: Cosmic voids occupy most of the universe's volume, yet galaxy formation inside them is poorly understood: void galaxies appear systematically different (bluer, less evolved), and tests of gravity in low-density environments are weak. Simulations struggle with void statistics, and modified-gravity theories predict distinctive void phenomena that have not been cleanly tested. Modified gravity theories like f(R) predict enhanced structure in voids, making void statistics a promising but underused test.
why_it_blocks: Voids are the most under-dense laboratories for gravity and galaxy formation, and they are under-exploited.
current_state: DESI's huge volume is enabling precision void statistics; void-based gravity tests are an active but immature program. DESI's void catalog, the largest ever assembled, is only beginning to be exploited for fundamental physics.

sources.title: DESI 2024 VI: Cosmological Constraints from BAO Measurements
